svg.title: Willow Creek Food Bank: current digital connections
svg.desc: A fictional practice map of the food bank's current systems. Two food-bank-owned laptops are used by Maya and Jordan and stay in the building. They and the check-in tablet connect to the building’s staff Wi-Fi. Renee configures the devices and accounts after Maya approves changes. The laptops have standard staff accounts, automatic updates, encrypted storage, and automatic screen locking. The tablet has a limited account and no permission to read stock records; sharing Wi-Fi does not imply the same permissions. The router and firewall connect by wire to a network switch. A local inventory server, a small computer storing food stock records, and a shared printer connect to that switch by wire. Staff accounts may use the stock records. Visitors use a separate guest Wi-Fi network; firewall rules allow Internet access but block the staff devices, server, and printer. Six of the eighteen volunteers work from home using personal devices and home Internet to access Google Workspace Gmail and the Drive Donor Answers folder. They have no VPN or connection to the local inventory server. Donors read current donation information on the public WordPress.com website and email questions to the food bank. Google operates the underlying computers, storage, and network for Google Workspace; the food bank manages its accounts, roles, and sharing. WordPress.com is hosted by Automattic; the food bank publishes its website content. An AI assistant is proposed but is not installed or enabled, and has no current connection in this map. Colored dashed boxes distinguish staff, guest, personal-device, and provider trust boundaries. Clinic scope is a separate agreement focused on donor replies and current donation guidance, Gmail and Drive access, website publishing, and the relevant food-bank device and network settings. The local stock server, printer, switch, check-in tablet, and guest Wi-Fi are context: they explain the surrounding system, but their configurations are reviewed only with an agreed reason and expanded scope. Whether stock records inform donation-guidance updates remains a question; no direct integration is assumed. A map does not authorize inspection. Personal-device settings and provider infrastructure are outside the review. Provider infrastructure is outside the client's control. No IP addresses or secrets are shown.
